newsitem.title: UK: Britannic says to speed up pension review.
newsitem.headline: Britannic says to speed up pension review.

text.p: Britannic Assurance on Tuesday promised to speed-up the review and settlement of cases of pension mis-selling as the insurer reported a jump in profits for 1996.
The company admitted it had some 13,000 priority review cases but said that the substantial resources committed to resolving the issue would help accelerate the process.
The industry has come under increasing criticism for the delays in compensating victims of pensions misselling in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
As many as 1-1/2 million people may have been wrongly advised by the industry to take out personal pensions instead of staying in occupational schemes.
A 23 million stg boost related to February's announcement of a 209 million stg special bonus for policyholders helped lift pre-tax profits by 47 percent to 93.9 million stg.
The bonus resulted from a clarification of ownership of orphan assets - money surplus to policyholders' needs in the with-profit funds - with the Department of Trade & Industry (DTI).
Under the agreement with the DTI, 902 million stg of the 5.68 billion stg life fund has been attributed to shareholders.
That helped lift the dividend by 82 percent to 28 pence per share, which the company said would provide the basis for dividend increases in the future.

Following a strategic review of its businesses, Britanic said it would be looking to build on its brand, investment management, distribution skills and product development capabilities to deliver enhanced value to shareholders and policyholders.
